issues.display_title: Issue #1776: [Editor] Extract and clean up Babylon runtime lifecycle
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Separate Babylon.js runtime ownership from Angular application state and guarantee cleanup when the editor session ends.

Scope

  • Introduce a focused runtime service responsible for Engine, Scene, canvas, render loop, runtime nodes, and Babylon observables.
  • Define explicit initialization and disposal methods.
  • Stop the render loop and dispose scene/engine resources on editor teardown.
  • Remove registered window/document listeners, timers, and Babylon observable callbacks owned by the runtime.
  • Scope runtime ownership to the editor route/session where dependency constraints allow.
  • Keep serializable editor data in EditorSessionStore, not in the runtime service.
  • Add lifecycle tests using test doubles for initialization and idempotent disposal.

Out of scope

  • Visual changes to the editor.
  • Changing persisted exhibition data.
  • Rewriting individual Babylon editing operations unrelated to lifecycle ownership.

Acceptance criteria

  • Entering the editor creates one runtime session.
  • Leaving the editor stops rendering and disposes owned resources.
  • Re-entering the editor does not duplicate listeners or render loops.
  • Disposal is safe when initialization is partial or called more than once.
  • Babylon objects do not enter the Signals store.
  • Lifecycle tests and the required development build pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #1777: [Editor] Optimize Angular-Babylon change detection boundary
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Prevent the Babylon render loop and high-frequency pointer/camera work from triggering unnecessary Angular change detection.

Scope

  • Run the Babylon render loop and continuous runtime callbacks outside Angular's zone.
  • Re-enter Angular only when an observable UI state actually changes.
  • Keep live mesh, camera, and gizmo transforms inside Babylon during pointer movement.
  • Commit serializable transform state to Angular Signals at operation boundaries such as drag end, input commit, or undo/redo completion.
  • Throttle any genuinely required live UI readout to at most once per animation frame.
  • Add instrumentation or focused tests that verify state commits are bounded and behavior is preserved.

Out of scope

  • Changing rendering quality or Babylon optimization settings.
  • Replacing Zone.js application-wide.
  • Redesigning editor controls.

Acceptance criteria

  • The render loop executes outside Angular change detection.
  • Dragging and camera movement remain responsive and visually unchanged.
  • Persisted transform state is committed when an operation completes.
  • No Signal is updated on every render frame without a documented UI requirement.
  • Selection, validation, and save state still update the UI.
  • Focused tests and the required development build pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #1778: [Editor] Remove Redux dependencies and complete Signals migration
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Finish the editor state migration by removing Redux infrastructure after all active consumers have moved to Angular Signals.

Scope

  • Confirm no application code imports redux, redux-watch, or the legacy store service.
  • Delete the remaining Redux store and reducer files.
  • Remove Redux exports from shared service barrels.
  • Remove redux and redux-watch from package dependencies and lockfile.
  • Remove redux-watch from Angular CommonJS allow-list configuration.
  • Update or remove obsolete tests and documentation.
  • Run full dead-reference searches and regression verification.

Out of scope

  • Adding NgRx or another state-management dependency.
  • Changing Babylon.js runtime behavior beyond completed prerequisite issues.
  • New editor features.

Acceptance criteria

  • No Redux or redux-watch import/reference remains under src.
  • Redux dependencies are absent from package.json and the lockfile.
  • Angular build configuration no longer allow-lists redux-watch.
  • Editor selection, tabs, object controls, undo/redo, validation, and saving still work.
  • Relevant tests pass.
  • The required development build passes.
